0055f3be4a8a.text: Commander, we only have so much electricity. The computer wants it for science experiments, and life support wants it for the air. What do we power?

02a66fd598a4.text: We bring back lots of ice! The trip is tiring and the radiation hit is real.

056b830c6baf.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X8.7)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

06c6a0f479c6.text: Near the Moon's south pole the Sun stays low and some mountain tops are in sunlight almost all the time. Shackleton crater is there, too. That is why NASA's Artemis missions want to land near the south pole.

07d99965fcdd.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X1.0)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

0a4f5f390a7c.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,452 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 29 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

0b1a106f0969.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M4.0) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

0bc6c731161f.text: Night is coming and it will last 14 Earth days, with no sunlight. The battery can't do everything. Keep the heaters on, call Earth, or sleep mode?

0c2920985156.text: After an X1.8 flare, the Sun launches a giant cloud at ~2,112 km/s. It reaches Earth's area in about a day and will cause a severe G4 storm on 10 October. The Moon has no magnetic field to help.

1127041b56ce.text: A person needs about 3 kilograms of water every day. Space stations clean used water and drink it again. Nothing is wasted, because bringing water from Earth is very expensive.

1277b62d1005.text: Only the important systems run. It is quiet and dark, but we make it through.

131669d20f39.text: An M-class flare from AR 12673: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

143e5b716812.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,452 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

153f60a8a6a6.text: We talk to Earth for hours. But the heaters get less power, the plants freeze and the air system slows.

16271537650c.text: An M-class flare from AR 13842: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

1afdfe2d0e7b.text: We wait under thick regolith. We are safe, but the garden and the antenna are not tended all day.

1b0d4dbd8828.text: M-class flare (M2.1) from AR 13854. Light arrives in ~8 minutes, so there is almost no warning for the outpost.

1b293fe4750c.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 2,678 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

1b92477772e8.text: The plants perk up and grow. The electrolyser makes less oxygen today.

1bc078555ba0.text: The solar wind shakes Earth's magnetic field: a G5 (extreme) storm, Kp 9.0 out of 9. The Moon has no magnetic field of its own, so the outpost is fully exposed and radio signals to Earth get noisy.

1c78606eef8d.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M3.7) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

1cbca3dbf36f.text: I miss home. Radio waves fly at the speed of light, yet it takes 1.3 seconds to reach Earth. Let's study the radio and build a big dish. Then Earth can hear us!

21fb3ef4294f.text: Everybody gets a few sips. Both systems work, but neither is happy.

236b2fb86588.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X4.5)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

24ae1c968f61.text: The Moon has almost no air at all. If you took off your helmet outside, there would be nothing to breathe. That is why Tobish lives in a sealed habitat that keeps its own air inside.

24c4332c8700.text: NASA's OSDR is a big free library with results from space biology experiments, such as plants, cells and animals studied in space. Anyone can read it, even students. Tobish adds his data to it.

283e88f57117.text: An M-class flare from AR 13839: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

28e90f1e6b34.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Geomagnetic storm: extreme (G5)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

2a78c02e1bc1.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M1.4) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

2b69b9766ef7.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X9.3)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

2c2210959ee0.text: Electricity splits water into oxygen and hydrogen. The air is great, the plants droop.

2de4bcb68567.text: The solar wind shakes Earth's magnetic field: a G4 (severe) storm, Kp 8.7 out of 9. The Moon has no magnetic field of its own, so the outpost is fully exposed and radio signals to Earth get noisy.

2f54181383f7.text: Gravity on the Moon is only one sixth of Earth's gravity. A kid who weighs 30 kilograms on Earth would feel like 5 kilograms on the Moon. You could jump much higher!

319bd5f71501.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: A coronal mass ejection is heading for the Moon. Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

34f8be4db6da.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,585 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 26 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

38c19ba14c92.text: The X8.2 flare of 10 Sep fires fast protons straight at us (SEP). The same storm was measured on the surface of Mars by the Curiosity rover's RAD instrument. On the Moon there is no air: get to the shelter!

3980b331a6a0.text: A lunar night lasts about 14 Earth days, with no sunlight at all. We must store energy in batteries before it comes. Study the solar field and the greenhouse. Then our outpost becomes a colony!

3b271bdc391a.text: Our research is ready. If we send everything at once, the dish uses huge power. We can also send it in small pieces over days. What do we do?

3b664215fbde.text: Commander, you hear me? Good. I crashed on the Moon, but my computer works and you found me. The air will run out first. Help me study the habitat and build an oxygen generator. Let's breathe!

3d12e1584cb2.text: The battery is safe, but Earth hears nothing from us and starts to worry.

3d5382aab9c6.text: Water tanks around the habitat soak up the particles. It costs a lot of energy and some water.

3f1ccccef99d.text: In the wreckage he found seeds, materials… and a computer that still worked.

3fcaea4bb855.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M9.1) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

43c96e0dbd75.text: We seal the room, but air slowly escapes before we do.

4475759e1f50.text: An M-class flare from AR 13685: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

44cb451820e1.text: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth. The other side, the far side, never faces us, so the Moon itself blocks radio waves. A far-side base needs a relay satellite to pass messages along.

45b978a6480d.text: Mission Control, if anyone can hear me… I need a commander.

4611b6e6eed3.text: An M-class flare from AR 13663: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

48029d724caf.text: Data sent! Mission Control cheers. I will stay here and contribute to humankind. Thank you for being my commander. A city grows on the Moon.

48ecc500ad49.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,585 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

4967c0572e4b.text: Sound cannot travel through empty space, but radio waves can. They move at the speed of light, the fastest speed there is. That is how Tobish talks to Earth.

4a070aa0c508.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M8.2) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

4a2f6e2f010c.text: The habitat and the plants stay warm. The radio is switched off to save power.

4b855a413984.text: Plants use light, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar, and they give off oxygen. A greenhouse on the Moon gives Tobish food and a little fresh air at the same time.

4eb9f549cced.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X1.6)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

4f3d50d9e30c.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M2.4) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

4f51432f964a.text: Dirty panels make less power, and the battery drops.

52580d29a516.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,535 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

53dbbc5430ee.text: If Tobish says hello and Mission Control answers right away, he waits about 2.6 seconds for the reply. The message goes there and back, so the wait is double.

55a2df274a41.text: In space, soil and water float away. So astronauts plant seeds in little 'pillows' that hold everything in place. The roots find the water inside, and the plants grow.

566345256f57.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,124 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 37 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

574ada49e3bf.text: The ship crashed on the Moon. Tobish was alone. No rescue. No second chance.

57bd72882a5e.text: The experiments give great data, but the air scrubbers slow down and the oxygen drops.

5847661b6334.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X5.8)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

58edcc56ca58.text: M-class flare (M9.1) from AR 13663. Light arrives in ~8 minutes, so there is almost no warning for the outpost.

5c2a940b561b.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,184 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

5e3dc7cb2330.text: Launch day. Everything was perfect. Until…

600be50d0183.text: The big dish is nearly ready! A full video call to Mission Control burns a lot of battery. A short text is cheap. Or we stay quiet.

613444b79b0d.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,184 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 35 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

61a4a28d1134.text: On the Moon the night lasts about two weeks. Plants cannot grow in the dark, so the greenhouse uses LED grow lights. The Veggie garden on the space station uses red, blue and green LEDs.

66b83e4be7c0.text: The Moon is about 384,400 kilometres from Earth. Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so a message from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth. That is a tiny wait.

696c5f36f463.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,148 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

6caddf10e89f.text: A Chinese lander called Chang'e-4 measured the radiation on the far side of the Moon. It is about 200 times more than on Earth's surface. That is why we need a shelter.

6e8cc0c988ff.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Geomagnetic storm: severe (G4)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

6f1c5acd0762.text: Outside the habitat there is no air pushing on you. So the habitat walls are strong and sealed tight. Inside, the air is like on Earth: about 21 percent of it is oxygen.

6f321d4e4903.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Geomagnetic storm (G2, Kp 6.0) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

6f4127103369.text: You breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide. The Moon has no air to breathe, so the habitat must make oxygen and clean the carbon dioxide away. One person uses almost 1 kilogram of oxygen every day.

708323b27803.text: The Sun flashes an X-class flare (AR 13664). Light and X-rays arrive in 8 minutes; energetic particles may come minutes to hours later.

7432becdede4.text: The solar wind shakes Earth's magnetic field: a G2 (moderate) storm, Kp 6.0 out of 9. The Moon has no magnetic field of its own, so the outpost is fully exposed and radio signals to Earth get noisy.

756e9de2b25b.text: The solar wind shakes Earth's magnetic field: a G4 (severe) storm, Kp 8.0 out of 9. The Moon has no magnetic field of its own, so the outpost is fully exposed and radio signals to Earth get noisy.

758d8c28a88e.text: X-class flare! Its light needs only ~8 minutes to cross space. The outpost has no magnetic field or thick air to help, so the radiation shield takes a big hit.

7616efc68e68.text: Artemis is NASA's program to send people back to the Moon. The Artemis II crew flew around the Moon in April 2026 and took this photo of Earth rising over the Moon. Next come landings near the south pole.

76181fff2123.text: Mayday! Mayday! We are going down!

76fada648b63.text: At twenty-four, Tobish graduated. And NASA chose him as its youngest astronaut.

777f5b55fe6f.text: One day, I will be a part of it.

778770d9f928.text: NASA's DONKI is a database where scientists record what the Sun does: flares, giant clouds and storms. Watching the Sun gives a warning, so Tobish can hide before the particles arrive.

77ef810ca094.text: Nice to meet you, Commander! Let's build a home on the Moon, together.

7872eb5df9d0.text: A coronal mass ejection, or CME, is a giant cloud of charged gas thrown out by the Sun. It is slower than light and needs about 1 to 3 days to reach the Moon and Earth. That gives time to get ready.

78a216c483e4.text: Rock and dirt block radiation. If the shelter is covered with a thick pile of Moon dust, called regolith, less radiation gets in. Water tanks also help, because water is a good radiation blocker.

7a54fe9cf2a9.text: NASA's Deep Space Network has giant dish antennas in 3 places: California, Spain and Australia. Because Earth spins, at least one dish can always see the Moon, even at night.

7e1961bb65bb.text: The air scrubbers run at full speed and the cabin smells fresh. The experiments wait.

7f274cb9ee80.text: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen. With electricity, a machine can split water apart and set the oxygen free for us to breathe. There is frozen water in dark craters near the Moon's poles.

7fb0177caed0.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,625 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 26 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

7fba1e8a9b4a.text: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. The panels work all day, but they stop at night. Batteries store extra energy in the day so the lights and machines keep running in the dark.

80be15dd818a.text: Moon dust is tiny and sharp. It sticks to space suits, like Commander Cernan's in the photo, and it sneaks inside. Filters in the habitat must catch the dust so we do not breathe it.

80c032786fe9.text: A tiny space rock hit the habitat wall. The Moon has no air to slow it down. There is a small air leak!

82c0f9fa6e80.text: The rover brings ice home safely. It uses a lot of battery.

83e3b12a1cd9.text: M-class flare (M2.4) from AR 13842. Light arrives in ~8 minutes, so there is almost no warning for the outpost.

8599f53f9d90.text: An M-class flare from AR 13654: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

878c20c0a542.text: The storm shelter is ready. A thick layer of regolith, the Moon's own dust, now blocks much of the radiation.

87c62d0c6f0d.text: Green leaves on the Moon! The garden gives me fresh food, and every plant breathes out a little oxygen.

885074bd6611.text: Astronauts on the space station grew red lettuce with a garden called Veggie. In 2015 the crew ate it fresh in space for the first time. If lettuce grows in space, it can grow on the Moon too.

8973282343a2.text: Lettuce usually needs about 4 weeks, or 28 days, to grow. Scientists found a clever trick: start the seedlings in a small nursery, then move them. That can cut the time to about 2 weeks.

9052f72a916f.text: I found seeds in the wreckage! Plants make food and oxygen, but they need light, water and care. Visit the greenhouse and the solar panels so we can grow the first Moon garden.

93bf8fc03831.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 2,678 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 16 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

968e05efe682.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,148 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 36 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

96a013bf1477.text: The solar wind shakes Earth's magnetic field: a G2 (moderate) storm, Kp 6.7 out of 9. The Moon has no magnetic field of its own, so the outpost is fully exposed and radio signals to Earth get noisy.

9725bac42e3e.text: The tank keeps the pressure steady while we wait for the repair.

989684d310d7.text: The oxygen generator hums. Electrolysis splits water into oxygen and hydrogen, and now I can breathe easy!

9925e3f1a22e.text: A small C-class flare (C7.7) from no numbered region. Light from it reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes, but this one is weak. The shield only loses a little.

9a14d1a62aa9.text: We have only a little water. The plants are thirsty, but the electrolyser also needs water to make oxygen. We can't do both fully!

9a9dc7be8b9c.text: I came here to do research and learn new things about the Moon and space. I found this working computer, and now I can send my data back to NASA. I will stay here and contribute to humankind.

9c5ccef8187a.text: So he studied. Every night. Mathematics. Physics. Astronomy.

9ce425a33da8.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M1.5) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

9cebf3dcc33f.text: This is it, Commander. Years of dreams brought me here. Let's finish the research in the lab and send all the data to NASA. Then people on Earth can learn from the Moon.

9e13e4c0b470.text: On Earth, thick air and a magnetic field work like an umbrella against space radiation. The Moon has no thick air and no global magnetic field. So radiation reaches the ground.

9f5257cceac0.text: The big dish points at Earth. I hear Mission Control! Every word arrives after 1.3 seconds.

a38b242d94ae.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M3.4) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

a4d1014adef2.text: The Sun throws out a giant cloud of charged gas at about 1,535 km/s. Travelling that fast it would cross the ~150 million km to the Earth–Moon area in roughly 27 hours. Radio signals and shields feel it.

a9e6ee911acd.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Radiation storm! (solar energetic particles) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

aac4b41183c5.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X2.1)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

adeba55b7988.text: Fast protons from the Sun race to the Moon within tens of minutes to hours. Unlike light they are bits of matter, and they can damage cells. Time to head for the shelter!

afce8e017939.text: The Moon turns very slowly. It spins around just once while it goes around Earth, which takes about a month. So the Sun takes about two weeks to cross the sky and another two weeks to be gone.

b039424c34f2.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M2.5) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

b0f460d0a073.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M1.9) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

b26f04a90d92.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,124 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

b324dd873a7a.text: Sunlight is very fast, but the Sun is very far. It takes about 8 minutes for light to reach the Moon, the same as for Earth. A burst of light from the Sun reaches us after 8 minutes.

babc4a941da1.text: A flare from AR 3664 has launched fast protons (SEP). They reach the Moon within tens of minutes to hours. Time to head for the shelter!

bbe188ee2cad.text: Half of the power goes to each. A little more air and a little more data.

be6fa7cf1d66.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M2.1) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

beb88cd13863.text: A glittering rock lies near the base. It could tell us how the Moon formed! Collecting it outside is risky.

c53d404d5cb5.text: The batteries are full and new modules are up. We are not an outpost anymore. We are a colony!

c639d095f31b.text: We'll try again, Commander. Every astronaut learns from mistakes.

c6e4b0cda11b.text: Orion is the spacecraft that carries Artemis astronauts. In 2022 an Orion without people on board flew past the Moon on the Artemis I test flight and photographed its far side.

c7aeea7bf676.text: The Sun flashes an X-class flare (AR 13842). Light and X-rays arrive in 8 minutes; energetic particles may come minutes to hours later.

c863eee5f979.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Strong solar flare (M3.6) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

c9643339a0dd.text: With no air to hold in warmth, the Moon gets very hot and very cold. At noon near the equator it is about +120 degrees Celsius. At night it drops to about -170 degrees Celsius.

ca43c6974cbb.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X9.0)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

cc0b1694ff78.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X3.4)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

cd24bb64f890.text: The Sun sends storms of fast particles. Earth has an atmosphere and a magnetic field, but the Moon does not. We need a shelter under Moon dust. Study radiation, then we build it. Stay sharp!

cf1ededde621.text: One day on the Moon lasts about two weeks on Earth. That is about 14.75 Earth days of sunshine, then about 14.75 days of darkness. Tobish needs power for both.

cf8999bec95d.text: We rest and save breath. The rock waits for another day.

cfaeebf8e894.text: When he was ten years old, a boy named Tobish watched a rocket launch on TV.

d019402bba86.text: We see Earth's engineers smile, with a 1.3 second delay. The battery drops a lot.

d055750fdede.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 1,625 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

d1d41625a75a.text: X9.3: the strongest flare of the whole 2017 cycle. X-rays arrive in 8 minutes; a fast cloud (CME, 1,881 km/s) follows. The outpost has no air or magnetic field to help.

d20f1f9259e4.text: Sometimes the Sun lets off a giant flash called a solar flare. Its light and X-rays zoom to the Moon in about 8 minutes. The Moon has no thick air to block them.

d2e729a2b9a9.text: Small packets fly to Earth all week. It is slower but gentle on the batteries.

d641b3ecab09.text: Until the impossible began to look like a plan.

d66914010e59.text: Mission Control! The engines are failing! We are losing control!

d66a11c6238c.text: A great sample! The walk costs air and gives some radiation.

d854727b6cdb.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X7.1)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

da01aac159f1.text: The camera sees the rock's shape and colour. We learn a little.

dd4009985cdc.text: A small message flies to Earth. It costs little and it still counts!

dd762cb6685d.text: Only oxygen, water, food… and his mind.

dda10e27403e.text: We fix some systems first. The data waits a little longer.

ddd360ffe276.text: An M-class flare from AR 13848: a flash of X-rays that reaches the Moon in about 8 minutes. Medium size, but the Moon has no air to soften it.

de652cb0a244.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Giant solar flare (X1.3)! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

e181c5595d8f.text: The Sun flashes an X-class flare (AR 13663). Light and X-rays arrive in 8 minutes; energetic particles may come minutes to hours later.

e3fd47db345e.text: The rover scanner sees water ice in a dark crater. Ice means water, water means air and food. But it's a long way off.

e48f2080e205.text: M-class flare (M2.1) from AR 13852. Light arrives in ~8 minutes, so there is almost no warning for the outpost.

e56f8a49aa6b.text: The leak is sealed. The spacewalk costs power and some radiation.

e572e03629a4.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Huge solar cloud (CME) at 2,112 km/s! Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

e8d0b8d28fa1.text: X8.7: the biggest flare of this storm series. Its light and X-rays hit the Moon in about 8 minutes. A fast cloud (CME) leaves at the same time and heads toward Earth.

e9697b186d74.text: Real garden soil has bits of old plants and tiny living things. Moon dust is crushed rock and has none of that. Scientists once grew small plants in real Apollo Moon dust, but the plants were weaker than normal.

eb9942e366ca.text: The panels shine again, but the walk outside costs oxygen and gives some radiation.

ed244bccc525.text: Science gets better when many people can see the numbers. If Tobish sends his plant and radiation data to Earth, scientists everywhere can study it and help future explorers.

ef8aa2d839ac.text: We finish the repairs, but the suit takes a lot of radiation. The base shield is weak after this.

efd9b7cf6496.text: Sticky Moon dust covers our solar panels. Less sunlight reaches them. How do we clean them?

f1ab6f838551.text: Astronauts on the space station float because they are falling around Earth. Without gravity, bones and muscles get weak. So astronauts exercise about 2 hours every day, even on a special treadmill.

f55522cf9009.text: A message to the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds. A message to Mars takes minutes, from about 3 to 22 minutes depending on where the planets are. Mars is much farther away.

f6c2032ed942.text: Commander, NASA's DONKI report says: Geomagnetic storm (G2, Kp 6.7) Fast particles are coming. What do we do? Hide, fix things outside, or power up the water wall?

faef61e8e572.text: We stay home and reuse every drop. A bit less than we need.

fc2c354bae92.text: Vibrations shake off some dust. A bit of radio noise comes with it.

fe126fdd7e8f.text: The big dish blasts all the data to Earth at once. The batteries are nearly flat afterwards.

fe71c10f697e.text: X9.0: the strongest flare of 2024. Light and X-rays reach the Moon in about 8 minutes, and the outpost has no air to block them.
